paper.title: Two-sided Competing Matching Recommendation Markets With Quota and Complementary Preferences Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Competing Matching under Complementary Preferences Recommendation problem (CMCPR)
unmapped: Two-sided many-to-one matching market: N firms (agents) and M types of workers (arms), K_m workers of type m
Centralized platform computes a stable matching each round; firms compete for workers
Firms have type-specific minimum quotas q_i^m and total quota Q_i (complementary preferences)
Workers' preferences over firms are known; firms' preferences unknown
Regret measured against the firm-optimal stable matching, summed over firms and types (Bayesian social welfare gap)
settings.definition_quote: If $p_i$ is matched with $a_j^m$ at time $t$, $p_i$ provides a noisy reward $y_{i,j}^m(t)$ which is assumed to be the true matching score $\mu_{i,j}^m$ plus a noise term ... sub-Gaussian ... Finally, define the Bayesian social welfare gap (BSWG) $\mathfrak{R}(T):= \mathbb{E}_{\theta \in \Theta}[\sum_{i=1}^{N}R_{i}(T,\theta)]$.

settings.name_in_paper: CMCPR incentive compatibility (single deviating Machiavelli firm)
unmapped: Strategic behaviour is by an agent (firm) deviating from MMTS recommendations, not by arms
Unique stable matching assumed (stated in discussion)
Bound on a single firm's firm-optimal regret for m-type workers
settings.definition_quote: Suppose all firms other than firm $p_{i}$ follow the preferences according to the $\mmts$ to the centralized platform.

algorithms.name: Multi-agent Multi-type Thompson Sampling (MMTS) with double matching

symbols.Q: total quota of all firms, sum_i Q_i
symbols.K_max: maximum number of workers of a single type, max_m K_m
symbols.K: total number of workers, sum_m K_m

source.label: thm: regret upper bound
source.quote: Assume $K_{\max} = \max\{K_{1},..., K_{M}\}, K = \sum_{m=1}^{M}K_{m}$, with probability $1-1/QT$, when all firms follow the $\mmts$ algorithm, firms together will suffer the Bayesian expected regret $$\mathfrak{R}(T) \leq 8Q\log(QT) \sqrt{K_{\max}T} + NK/Q.$$

results.notes: Paper states a Bayesian expected regret holding 'with probability 1-1/QT' (odd combination); recorded as high_probability as stated. Comparator is the firm-optimal stable matching, mapped to best_fixed_action. Theorem F.1 restates the same bound as 8 log(QT) sqrt(QK_max) sqrt(QT) + NK/Q.

symbols.R_IC: sum over super-optimal workers l (negative super gap Delta_bar_{i,l}^m) of Delta_bar_{i,l}^m times min over covers S^m of the achievable sub-matching set of sum over blocking triplets (C_{i,j,k'}^m + log(T)/kl(mu_{j,u_min}, mu_{j,k'})), with C = O((log T)^{-1/3})

conditions: all firms other than p_i follow MMTS

source.label: thm: IC
source.quote: Suppose all firms other than firm $p_{i}$ follow the preferences according to the $\mmts$ to the centralized platform. Then the following upper bound on firm $p_{i}$'s optimal regret for $m$-type workers holds: R_{i}^{m}(T,\theta) \geq \sum_{l: \overline{\Delta}_{i,l}^{m} < 0} \overline{\Delta}_{i,l}^{m}[...]

results.notes: Lower bound (negative, of order -O(log T)) on a deviating firm's regret, showing incentive compatibility; derived from Lemma 5.1 bound on expected number of matches with super-optimal workers. Statement text calls it an 'upper bound' but writes >=. Restated as Theorem G.1.
